runs.processNote: MAJOR: this run found three consecutive unmerged audit-state PRs (#44, #49, #51) all still open, each built on stale main because none had been merged, causing three straight runs to independently re-verify overlapping batches before discovering the duplication. To stop compounding this, this run's branch was reset to the tip of PR #51 (claude/charming-brown-yme6ae, the most complete of the three) rather than to stale main, so this run's PR is a strict superset of #44+#49+#51's changes plus this run's new champions-mindset batch -- merging this PR alone is sufficient, and #44/#49/#51 can then be closed as superseded. Flagged prominently to the user via notification given 3 unmerged PRs + 12 open untriaged issues is no longer a minor housekeeping note. Re-checked open content PRs #23, #24, #46, #47: all unchanged (same single commit each), findings still hold, nothing new to flag. CORRECTION (applied 2026-08-06 during PR review): the 'strict superset' claim above is FALSE. This branch was reset from PR #51's tip, but #51 was never built on #49 -- git merge-base confirms #51 is an ancestor of this branch while #44 and #49 are not. #49's dylan-014 content fix (the truncated-quote correction) was therefore NOT carried over, and closing #49 as superseded would have silently dropped it while this file continued to record it as fixed. Resolved by merging #49 into main FIRST, then merging main into this branch. #44 and #51 are genuinely superseded here (both state-file-only, and their run entries are carried forward above); #49 was not. PROCESS LESSON for future runs: do not assume a branch reset from another run's tip inherits every earlier run's changes. Verify with `git merge-base --is-ancestor <other-branch> HEAD` for EACH PR claimed as superseded, and diff the actual quote content -- not just the state file -- before recommending anything be closed.

Milne, Winnie-the-Pooh, Eeyore's line, corroborated via Wikisource Ch. 8 text), and kidlit-010 (Roald Dahl, Charlie and the Chocolate Factory, Oompa-Loompa TV song) all verified verbatim -- no issues. kidlit-007 (the Pooh/Piglet 'What's for breakfast?' / 'I wonder what's going to happen exciting today?' / 'It's the same thing' exchange) was stored as A. A. Milne, The House at Pooh Corner (1928). The prior run (issue #65, 2026-08-09) had already checked this exact quote and correctly found it's genuinely Milne's own text -- not Benjamin Hoff's invention, despite an AZQuotes listing that misattributes it to Hoff (author of The Tao of Pooh, which quotes the passage). This run independently re-derived the same authorship conclusion, but went one step further: cross-referencing standardebooks.org, americanliterature.com, and Wikisource all place this exact passage in Chapter 10 of Winnie-the-Pooh (1926) -- 'In Which Christopher Robin Gives Pooh a Party, and We Say Goodbye' -- not in The House at Pooh Corner (1928) as the collection (and issue #65's review) had it. Wrong-book citation, not a misattribution of authorship.
runs.resolution: kidlit-007 fixed in this run's PR: source corrected from 'The House at Pooh Corner (1928)' to 'Winnie-the-Pooh (1926)', quoteDate to 1926, notes updated with the chapter citation and a note debunking the AZQuotes/Hoff misattribution so it isn't rediscovered as a false lead by a future run. authorName (A. Lesson for future runs: an aggregator's attribution (AZQuotes, Goodreads, etc.) is exactly the kind of source this audit exists to distrust -- it should never be the sole basis for a 'correction' even when it looks like a clean lead; check for a prior audit finding on the same quote ID before trusting it. 0 open PRs and 0 open issues found at the start of this run -- the housekeeping backlog flagged in the 2026-08-05..08 runs is fully resolved (issue #65 is the most recent closed one).
